title: Standardized SPME-GC-MS Protocol for the Detection of Volatile and Semi-Volatile Compounds in Human Serum
author: Lilia C. Soler-Jiménez
materials: Precondition the DVB/CAR/PDMS fiber as per manufacturer instructions.
Compare VOC profiles between Chagas-positive and negative groups.

steps.title: Prepare Serum Sample
steps.instruction: Mix 100 µL of blood serum and 200 µL of HPLC-grade methanol in a 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Precipitate Proteins
steps.instruction: Vortex the mixture for 30 seconds and let it stand at room temperature for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Separate Supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample at 12,500 rpm for 10 minutes, then transfer the clear supernatant to a 0.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Store Supernatant
steps.instruction: If not analyzed immediately, store the supernatant at 4°C for up to 24 hours.

steps.title: Extract Compounds via SPME
steps.instruction: Extract compounds using a DVB/CAR/PDMS SPME fiber.

substeps.instruction: Introduce the fiber directly into the serum supernatant.
Allow extraction to proceed for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Optional: For volatile-only profiling, perform headspace extraction at 40 °C.

steps.title: Desorb Fiber in GC Inlet
steps.instruction: Immediately transfer the fiber to the GC inlet and desorb at 270 °C for 5 min in splitless mode.

steps.title: Run GC-MS Analysis
steps.instruction: Run GC-MS using the specified temperature program and acquire mass spectra in full scan mode (m/z 50–650).

steps.title: Process and Identify Data
steps.instruction: Analyze the resulting data to identify and quantify compounds.

substeps.instruction: Identify compounds using the NIST library (Salek et al 2013).
Normalize peak areas and calculate retention indices (Sun and Stremple 2003).

description: Troubleshooting Perform all extractions in triplicate to assess reproducibility. Regularly clean the injector port and replace the septum to avoid carryover. Ensure fibers are properly conditioned before use. Store samples and extracts cold to avoid degradation.
